_meta.role: Practical Guidance Store - per-issue action steps and official portal definitions. Highest change-rate, lowest legal-risk file of the three; kept separate so editing steps/URLs can never corrupt verified legal text.
_meta.population_status: SKELETON - no guidance or portals populated. Populated per issue only after taxonomy sign-off.
governance: CLAUDE.md Section 8 (action-step and portal rules), Section 7.2 (why three files).

Action steps are issue-specific (never generic domain boilerplate), most time-sensitive first, max 5, no FIR filing as primary advice, no criminal procedure steps. Curated by humans - an LLM must not freely generate legally sensitive procedure steps at request time.
Portals: only official government / regulator / statutory-authority portals. Conditional portals (e.g. a banking ombudsman) must carry a usage_condition and must not be returned unconditionally.
Wording in action steps must follow CLAUDE.md Section 10 (no 'you will win', no 'definitely applies', etc.).
consumed_by: Module 3 (Legal Intelligence Engine): given the detected issue_id, reads action_steps; resolves portal_ids against 'portals'; filters portals to those whose supported_issue_ids contain the issue_id; sorts by priority (immediate -> primary -> secondary); returns max 3.
Module 4 (Response Builder): places the returned steps/portals into the response contract fields 'action_steps' and 'portals'.
knowledge_base_loader: loads and reference-validates this file at startup (read-only at runtime).

<issue_id>._id_rule: issue_id must exist in issue_mappings.json (same signed-off taxonomy).
action_steps: array of 1-5 strings - ordered, issue-specific steps; index 0 is the most time-sensitive. Plain language, awareness-safe wording.
portal_ids: array of strings - each must resolve to an entry in 'portals'. Order here is informational; Module 3's priority sort decides final order.

<portal_id>._id_rule: portal_id is a stable snake_case string, e.g. 'cybercrime_gov_in'.
<portal_id>.portal_id: string - MUST equal the object key. Explicit self-identifier so records are safe to validate, iterate, and pass around detached from their key.
<portal_id>.name: string - official portal name
<portal_id>.official_url: string | null - confirmed official URL only; null until confirmed, never a placeholder
<portal_id>.purpose: string - what a citizen uses this portal for
<portal_id>.priority: enum: 'immediate' (time-sensitive, contact within ~24h) | 'primary' (main formal complaint avenue) | 'secondary' (alternative/supplementary)
<portal_id>.usage_condition: string | null - REQUIRED (non-null) for conditional portals; describes when this portal applies (e.g. only after an initial complaint to the bank). null means unconditional for its supported issues.
<portal_id>.official_source: string - owning authority, e.g. 'Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India'
supported_issue_ids: array of strings - issue IDs this portal supports; Module 3 filters on membership here

action_steps: Contact your bank immediately and report the unauthorised transaction. Ask the bank to block the card, account, or UPI ID involved to prevent further loss.
Call the national cyber crime helpline 1930 as soon as possible - early reporting improves the chance of freezing the fraudulent transfer.
Preserve all evidence: the caller's number, SMS alerts, transaction IDs, screenshots, and the exact time of the calls and debits.
File a written complaint on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal and keep the acknowledgment number for follow-up.
Follow up with your bank in writing about reversal or chargeback of the unauthorised transaction, and keep copies of every communication.
If any money was transferred because of the impersonation, contact your bank immediately and call the national cyber crime helpline 1930 to report the financial fraud.
Preserve evidence before it can be deleted: take screenshots of the fake profile or messages, and note the profile link, caller numbers, and dates and times.
Report the fake profile or account to the platform (social media site, messaging app, or website) using its impersonation reporting option and request its removal.
File a complaint on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal with the collected evidence and keep the acknowledgment number for follow-up.
Inform the people being contacted in your name - a simple warning message prevents relatives, friends, or colleagues from being cheated.
If you entered any password, PIN, or card details on the suspicious page, change those passwords immediately and contact your bank to block the card or account before further misuse.
If any money was debited, call the national cyber crime helpline 1930 right away - early reporting improves the chance of freezing the fraudulent transfer.
Do not click the link again or forward it. Preserve evidence: screenshots of the message and page, the sender's number or email address, and the link itself.
File a complaint on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal with the evidence and keep the acknowledgment number for follow-up.
Report the fraudulent SMS, call, or WhatsApp message on the Chakshu facility of Sanchar Saathi so the sender can be acted against.

If a loan, account, or transaction exists in your name that you never took, immediately inform the concerned bank, lender, or wallet company in writing that it is not yours and ask them to mark it as disputed.

File a complaint on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal with whatever proof you have (recovery calls, credit report entries, SIM details), and call the 1930 helpline if money was actually taken from you.
Check how many mobile connections exist in your name using the TAFCOP facility on Sanchar Saathi and report any SIM you did not take.
If your Aadhaar may have been misused, lock your Aadhaar biometrics through UIDAI's official service and raise a grievance with UIDAI.
Check your credit report for accounts you did not open, raise disputes with the credit bureau in writing, and keep every acknowledgment safely.

Try to recover the account immediately using the platform's official account-recovery option, then change the password and enable two-factor authentication on it and on any account that shared the same password.
If the account has saved cards, bank links, or wallet balances, inform your bank or the payment provider immediately, and call the 1930 cyber crime helpline if any money was taken.
Report the takeover to the platform through its hacked-account or compromised-account reporting form so the account can be secured or suspended.
Preserve evidence: screenshots of unauthorized activity, alert emails about password or recovery changes, and the dates and times you noticed the misuse.
File a complaint on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal with the evidence, and warn your contacts if the account is being used to message them.
Stop using the product and preserve it in its current condition along with the bill, warranty card, box, and photos or a video clearly showing the defect.
Complain to the seller and the manufacturer in writing (email or letter), ask for repair, replacement, or refund as per the warranty terms, and keep proof of your complaint.
If the seller does not resolve it, register a grievance with the National Consumer Helpline by calling 1915 or through its online portal.
If the issue remains unresolved, you can file a formal consumer complaint before the appropriate Consumer Commission, which can be done online through the e-daakhil facility.
Keep every receipt, service-visit record, and acknowledgment safely - they form the evidence for your complaint.

Send the seller or company a written refund demand (email or letter) stating the amount, the date of payment, the policy or promise you are relying on, and a clear deadline - keep proof that you sent it.
Collect and keep your payment proof: order confirmation, invoice, bank or UPI statement entry, and any screenshots of the refund policy or the refund promise.
Escalate to the platform's or company's grievance officer if the first-level support keeps closing your request without resolving it.
If it remains unresolved, register a grievance with the National Consumer Helpline by calling 1915 or through its online portal.
As the next step, you can file a formal consumer complaint before the appropriate Consumer Commission, which can be done online through the e-daakhil facility.
Save the advertisement itself before it disappears - screenshots, photos, or a recording of the ad, along with where and when you saw it, plus your purchase proof.
Complain in writing to the seller or advertiser pointing out the difference between what was advertised and what was delivered, and ask for the promised remedy - keep proof of your complaint.

Register a grievance with the National Consumer Helpline by calling 1915 or through its online portal - misleading advertisement complaints can also be taken up by the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA).
If it remains unresolved, you can file a formal consumer complaint before the appropriate Consumer Commission through the e-daakhil facility.
Keep all bills, packaging, and communications safely - your evidence needs to show the gap between the advertised claim and the reality.
Collect what was promised versus what was delivered: the agreement or receipt, advertisements or brochures, chats or emails, and photos or videos of the poor or incomplete work.
Complain to the service provider in writing describing the deficiency specifically, and ask for completion, rectification, or refund with a clear deadline - keep proof of the complaint.
Escalate to the provider's grievance or customer-care escalation channel if first-level support does not resolve it.
Register a grievance with the National Consumer Helpline by calling 1915 or through its online portal.
If it remains unresolved, you can file a formal consumer complaint before the appropriate Consumer Commission through the e-daakhil facility.
Keep the evidence of the practice: the bill or receipt, the product packaging showing the MRP, and photos or notes of what was charged versus what was promised.

Raise the issue with the seller in writing, point out the specific unfair practice (overcharging, wrong billing, forced bundling), and ask for a corrected bill or refund - keep proof of your complaint.
For overcharging above MRP or weight or measurement issues, you may also raise it with the Legal Metrology department of your state in addition to the consumer route.
Register a grievance with the National Consumer Helpline by calling 1915 or through its online portal.
If it remains unresolved, you can file a formal consumer complaint before the appropriate Consumer Commission through the e-daakhil facility.
Ask the detaining officer for the written detention order or seizure memo, and note the stated legal ground, the officer's details, and the date and time.
Collect and keep your vehicle documents - registration certificate, permit (if applicable), insurance, and driving licence - as producing valid papers is usually central to release.
Ask about the release procedure, any fee or fine payable, and insist on an official receipt for any amount you pay.
If you believe the detention or the process is improper, escalate in writing to the concerned transport authority or its grievance channel, keeping copies.
Keep every document, receipt, and communication safely as a record of the detention and the release steps.

cybercrime_gov_in.name: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal
cybercrime_gov_in.purpose: File complaints about cybercrime incidents, including online financial fraud, and track their status.
cybercrime_gov_in.official_source: Ministry of Home Affairs (Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre), Government of India

rbi_cms.name: RBI Complaint Management System (Integrated Ombudsman Scheme)
rbi_cms.purpose: Escalate a complaint about an unauthorised banking transaction against a bank or regulated entity.
rbi_cms.usage_condition: Use only if you have already complained to your bank about the unauthorised transaction and it has not been resolved satisfactorily within the bank's stipulated time (typically 30 days).

sanchar_saathi_chakshu.name: Sanchar Saathi - Chakshu (Report Suspected Fraud Communication)
sanchar_saathi_chakshu.purpose: Report suspected fraud calls, SMS, or WhatsApp communications, including impersonation of officials, companies, or known persons.
sanchar_saathi_chakshu.usage_condition: Use when the fraudulent communication (impersonation, fake link, or fraud attempt) came through a phone call, SMS, or WhatsApp, in addition to filing the main complaint on the cyber crime portal.
sanchar_saathi_chakshu.official_source: Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications, Government of India

sanchar_saathi_tafcop.name: Sanchar Saathi - TAFCOP (Know Mobile Connections in Your Name)
sanchar_saathi_tafcop.purpose: Check how many mobile connections have been issued in your name and report SIM cards you did not authorize.
sanchar_saathi_tafcop.usage_condition: Use when you suspect that SIM cards or mobile connections were taken in your name without your knowledge.
sanchar_saathi_tafcop.official_source: Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications, Government of India

uidai.name: UIDAI (Aadhaar) Official Portal
uidai.purpose: Lock or unlock Aadhaar biometrics and raise grievances about suspected misuse of your Aadhaar.
uidai.usage_condition: Use when the identity misuse involves, or may involve, your Aadhaar number or biometrics.
uidai.official_source: Unique Identification Authority of India, Government of India

consumer_helpline_ingram.name: National Consumer Helpline (INGRAM)
consumer_helpline_ingram.purpose: Register a consumer grievance (helpline 1915 or online) for guidance and company-level resolution before formal proceedings.
consumer_helpline_ingram.official_source: Department of Consumer Affairs, Government of India

edaakhil.name: e-daakhil (Online Consumer Commission Complaint Filing)
edaakhil.purpose: File a formal consumer complaint online before the appropriate Consumer Commission.
edaakhil.usage_condition: Use when the complaint is not resolved through the seller or the National Consumer Helpline and you want to file a formal complaint before a Consumer Commission.
edaakhil.official_source: National Informatics Centre for the Consumer Commissions, Government of India

parivahan.name: Parivahan (Ministry of Road Transport and Highways)
parivahan.purpose: Access vehicle and transport-related services and grievance options of the transport department.
parivahan.usage_condition: Use for transport-department services or to escalate a grievance about the detention process, in addition to dealing with the detaining authority directly.
parivahan.official_source: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Government of India
